title: Compatible closed monoidal comparisons for open restriction
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an open, and suppose its specified derived category and the derived category of the over-site of U have morphism universe w [def-pc-derived-category]. Use the standard derived category of modules on U.toScheme in morphism universe u+1. Let E be the derived functor of Modules.overEquiv U [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and R the composite of derived over-site restriction with E. Let H_X and H_U be the fixed derived internal Hom functors [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and e_X and e_U the canonical tensor-Hom bijections [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] for the specified tensor structures [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. There exists a strong monoidal structure m on R, and isomorphisms h(K,N):R(H_X(K,N)) ≅ H_U(RK,RN) for all K,N, such that for every ξ:A → H_X(K,N), e_U(Rξ;h(K,N).hom)=μ_m(A,K).hom;R(e_X(ξ)). This asserts preservation of uncurrying, including the tensor-unit comparison carried by m, and does not assert the square for the adjunct defining canonical dual evaluation.

proof.text: The over-site equivalence identifies a module over V→U with the same module on the corresponding open of U.toScheme. Its inverse restores those sections, so both composites are naturally isomorphic to the identity. The exact derived equivalence is obtained by applying its termwise complex functor and localization; its factorization is mapDerivedCategoryFactors. Different localization universes are compared by the universal property of localization.

Choose K-flat tensor representatives globally. Exact open restriction preserves their K-flatness and identifies each tensor term and coproduct total degree with the restricted term. Localize these comparisons. The tensor unit is the structure sheaf in degree zero, and restriction and overEquiv identify it with the corresponding unit on the open scheme. Use the termwise tensor naturality statement to descend natural comparisons. For coherence, transport the strong monoidal structure on ordinary pullback along overFunctorEquiv and restrictFunctorIsoPullback (the cited pullback monoidal statement supplies its unit and associativity laws), then sum the resulting tensorators on total complexes. These give natural tensor and unit comparisons; their associativity and unit laws hold on each pure tensor before localization.

Compute derived internal Hom on the fixed functorial K-injective target. Its restriction is K-injective. The product Hom restriction comparison sends every local linear map to its restriction and respects differentials. Apply the exact over-equivalence and localization factorization to obtain natural Hom comparisons, for N and for the tensor unit.

The uncurrying of each Hom-complex map is fixed on every total-tensor summand by the canonical representative equation. Restriction acts on its local linear maps, so uncurrying before or after the tensor and Hom comparisons gives identical components. By the cited K-injective Hom lemma, Hom of a K-flat complex with a K-injective complex is K-injective. Maps into it represent all derived maps modulo homotopy; use common K-flat resolutions and naturality for arbitrary arguments. Localization through E permits the independently specified universes. This gives the displayed uncurrying equation, without proving the associator and right-unitor composite square of the parent item.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_openRestriction_closedMonoidal (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] :
    let E := (Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let R := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ E
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace) X.sheaf
    let HU := derivedInternalHom
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology U.toScheme.toRingedSpace) U.toScheme.sheaf
    ∃ m : R.Monoidal,
      letI := m
      ∃ h : ∀ K N : schemeDerivedCategory X,
        R.obj (H.obj (op K, N)) ≅ HU.obj (op (R.obj K), R.obj N),
        ∀ A K N (ξ : A ⟶ H.obj (op K, N)),
          schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv U.toScheme (R.obj A) (R.obj K) (R.obj N)
            (R.map ξ ≫ (h K N).hom) =
          (Functor.Monoidal.μIso R A K).hom ≫
            R.map (schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv X A K N ξ)
